unit.unit_name: Introduction to Functions and Rates of Change
learning_goals: Describe functions through equations, graphs, domains, ranges, and interval notation
Analyze absolute value, parent, transformed, inverse, and piecewise functions
Calculate and interpret average rate of change and estimate instantaneous rate of change

analysis_summary.notes: This blueprint documents the Version 5 practice variation. The underlying sample pattern is unofficial; no source question is copied.

sections.title: Multiple choice
sections.instructions: Circle one answer for each one-mark question.

sections.title: Multipart Unit 1 questions
sections.instructions: Show reasoning, label sketches and diagrams, and use interval notation where requested.

ordering_rules: Start with ten one-mark multiple-choice questions.
Follow with eight consecutive multipart questions with mark allocation 9, 6, 5, 5, 7, 8, 5, 5.
Supply original diagrams for the circular ride and secant-tangent questions.
Give students room for graphing and calculations in the printable PDF.

topic_distribution.topic: Average and instantaneous rates of change

progression_notes: Multiple choice includes combined constraints and one-step reasoning.
Multipart questions move from a curved piecewise branch to transformations and inverse restrictions.
Context and diagram questions require quarter-turn points and interpretation of rates.

diagram_expectations: Use original labelled observation-wheel diagram for domain/range reasoning
Use original secant/tangent graph for rate interpretation
Require labelled axes and open/closed endpoints in student sketches
Blank graph grids and ruled calculation space in the student PDF

trap_patterns.description: Confusing open and closed interval or piecewise endpoints
Using k instead of 1/k in a point mapping
Confusing inverse with reciprocal or omitting a domain restriction
Confusing secant slope with tangent slope or omitting units

generation_rules.variation_policy: Preserve Version 4 section count and marks, but write new functions, values, contexts, and distractors with modestly increased reasoning demand.
freshness_requirements: No verbatim textbook or public sample stems
constraints: Stay within the supplied Unit 1 index.

Use original diagrams for circular ride and secant-tangent questions.
